V-ENCLOSURE.evidence: Dining area is bounded by the building on the left, a wall on the right, and a pergola overhead, but is open on the top and bottom sides. The fire pit area is open on three sides.

V-FOCAL.evidence: Large citrus tree in the lower-left corner is the dominant element, with the fire pit and dining pergola positioned as secondary features.

V-AXIS.evidence: Main gravel path leads directly to house doors and dining area; secondary paths connect fire pit, seating, and herb garden. All circulation routes terminate at functional features.

V-RHYTHM.evidence: Top right corner shows a distinct mass of four small trees/shrubs. Bottom left shows a large canopy tree with a drift of three shrubs and a cluster of ground cover. The 'herbs' bed is a single mass. Repetition is evident in the grouping strategy.

V-LAYERING.evidence: Top right corner shows canopy trees overlapping shrubs and ground cover. Bottom left shows a large canopy tree with shrubs and ground cover beneath. Multiple planting zones exhibit this vertical layering.

V-ROOMS.evidence: Multiple distinct zones with different floor surfaces: gravel fire pit area, paved dining under pergola, paved standing/BBO area, and separate herb bed.

V-OVERALL.evidence: Clear zoning into distinct rooms (dining, fire pit, standing/BBQ, citrus, herbs), defined edges via walls and paving, and structured planting masses (canopy tree, shrub cluster, ground cover) create a cohesive, designed landscape.
